nodes.label: polar_lib.cjs (shared geometry helper)
nodes.rationale: Provides polar(), annularWedgePath(), angularHalfWidthAt(), boundsSymmetric()/boundsAsymmetric(), drawArc(). Was missing from the repo until 2026-10-16 even though two committed scripts already depended on it.

nodes.label: Family 1 — generation-ladder diagrams
nodes.rationale: Shows the full dyadic subdivision (radius = generation depth). No stroke between cells and RADIAL_GAP=0 between generation rings -- changed 2026-10-16 because the original 1px-stroke-plus-1px-gap convention produced a visually uncomfortable dense grid of fine lines at G7/G8 density (up to 128 cells/ring, 8 rings/arc).

nodes.label: Family 2 — full-resolution "quick ref" diagrams
nodes.rationale: Shows the finished primary-to-primary gradient at full resolution (257 points, G0-G8 merged and sorted by t) as one band per arc -- no stroke between cells since at 257 abutting cells a stroke rendered as washed-out moire.

nodes.label: Diagram line-removal experiment (tried and reverted, 2026-10-16)
nodes.rationale: Removing the per-cell stroke and inter-generation-ring gap was tried to fix a moire/dense-grid-of-lines problem on screen; technique itself worked (confirmed via polar pixel-sampling) but Ray reverted it anyway purely on preference ('that diagram did not need the white lines removed... one thing at a time') -- a case where the fix succeeded technically but wasn't wanted.

nodes.label: RENDER_SCALE gotcha (viewBox vs CSS size mismatch)
nodes.norm_label: render_scale gotcha (viewbox vs css size mismatch)
nodes.rationale: build_summary_rings.cjs's canvas grew from 1800 to 3000 viewBox units (to fit three rings without clipping) but its CSS render size stayed 1800px, so 1 viewBox unit renders as only 0.6 actual on-screen px. Any gap specified as a direct on-screen px target must go through an explicit RENDER_SCALE=1800/3000 correction before conversion to viewBox units, or a bare mm-based constant will be silently 0.6x too small once rendered.

nodes.label: SEAM_EPS_DEG angular-overlap seam fix
nodes.rationale: Even without a stroke, adjacent flat-fill wedges don't rasterise to a perfectly shared edge -- sub-pixel rounding leaves a hairline seam that shimmers on screen. Fixed by giving every cell a tiny angular overlap with its neighbours: 0.03deg for Family 2 (confirmed small enough not to eat into the narrowest real gap, ~15x smaller), 0.08deg for Family 1 (needed larger after polar pixel-sampling showed 0.03 still left ~1% residual near-white hits at Level 2's narrower cell width).

nodes.label: Level 2 cross-arc "rescue" method
nodes.rationale: A muted/earthy target that doesn't fit a pure Level 1 arc often fits a Level 2 cross-arc mix (e.g. green x violet) instead -- blending with an adjacent-family arc at the same t/generation knocks chroma and value down together. Recommended as the first thing to check before reaching for any kind of dechroma transform.

nodes.label: Olive/dechroma dead end (Chapter 5 pre-thinking)
nodes.rationale: A pure value-held chroma reduction from a Level 1 arc point cannot reach a muted target like Olive because the YgB arc's hue and lightness are coupled (hue rotates toward blue-green as lightness drops) -- the nearest-hue arc point sits at the wrong lightness entirely. Resolved by using the Level 2 cross-arc rescue method instead.

nodes.label: build_level2_standalone.cjs (currently not runnable)
nodes.rationale: Depends on level2_standalone_rows.json, which was never migrated into this repo, and uses a third, different gap convention (flat WIDE_HALF=3deg between zones, linear-width SEAM_LINEAR_HALF=2.8 within a pair) that predates the Level 1+2 combo's convention.

nodes.label: "Hue gap + tint (combo)" taxonomy category
nodes.rationale: Found by widening the hue-gap rule to not require a small dL -- caught pencils with a real hue gap AND a lightness gap simultaneously that had been mislabeled pure 'tint' because dL numerically dominated the old dL-vs-dC tiebreak. 100% of these resolve against the full value-shifted ladder, concentrated on the YgB x BvR Level 2 cross-arc's pastel region.

nodes.label: Level 4 tint ladder (toward white)
nodes.rationale: Formalizes 19 fixed tint steps per arc point (mixSpectral toward white, no new anchors). Originally built on Level 1+Level 2 only (reasoning: Level 3 is already a borrowed-depth mix, so tinting it would just retrace ground L1/L2 cover) -- reversed 2026-10-18 after real data showed 8 of a new taxonomy category needed Level 3 tints specifically, since the three-way mix sits at a genuinely different point in colour space than any L1/L2 tint reaches.

nodes.label: Level 2 diagram stacked-radial layout (2026-10-17)
nodes.rationale: Reworked from side-by-side like/flipped (hard to compare) to Level1-inner/like-middle/flipped-outer because real pencils land on 'flipped' roughly 2x as often as 'like' (64%/36% split) -- not because either pairing is more correct, they're equally valid different mixes.

nodes.label: Pigment Ancestry Model (Colour Family Arc System)
nodes.norm_label: pigment ancestry model (colour family arc system)

nodes.label: Eyedropper (exact point sampling)
nodes.rationale: Full-resolution pixel sampling (not the downscaled clustering copy) to match how a painter actually works from a reference: pick the spot, not an algorithm's average.

nodes.label: "I'm feeling lucky" button
nodes.rationale: Generates a random starting colour directly in OKLCH space (not RGB) so chroma is taken as a fraction of what each hue can hold before clipping, keeping every hue comparably vivid instead of always-muted yellows next to always-maxed blues.

nodes.label: k-means clustering in OKLab (photo extraction)
nodes.rationale: Samples spread across shadows/midtones/highlights rather than averaged into mud; every swatch stays a real pixel, never a synthetic blend.

nodes.label: Palette Health Score
nodes.rationale: Built from measurable colour science (WCAG contrast, OKLab spacing, temperature, saturation rhythm, etc.) rather than a single opaque AI-generated number, so dimensions and weights can be justified and changed per goal.

nodes.label: Polychromos pencil matching
nodes.rationale: Matching runs in OKLab rather than raw RGB distance so 'closest' tracks how the eye actually reads colour difference.

nodes.label: Running it (single-file, no-build deployment)
nodes.rationale: Everything (markup, styles, colour math, even the base64-embedded logo) lives in one index.html so the page stays dependency-free with no separate asset to host.

nodes.label: WCAG 2.x contrast math
nodes.rationale: Follows the WCAG 2.x relative-luminance formula for accessible/legible colour pairings.

nodes.label: Level 3 "Arc1 — aligned" dropped
nodes.rationale: Every Level 1 arc pairs a warm anchor from one family with a cool anchor from another, so the 'aligned' (no-flip) three-way combination always mixes warm+cool and never settles toward a clean warm or cool result -- permanently medium-muted (chroma 28.7, range 22.2-41.0 vs 0.4-70.3 for the three flipped arcs). Rescued zero book-scope pencils before being dropped; verified the drop changes coverage not at all (771/1150, 846/1294, identical).

nodes.label: ΔE ≤ 15.3 fit threshold (CIE76, D65)
nodes.rationale: Raised from 14 to 15.3 at anchor sign-off; chosen as the one threshold used everywhere afterward for consistency, despite known CIE76 non-uniformity (same ΔE is a bigger perceptual shift on low-chroma colours than high-chroma ones).

nodes.label: P3-vs-sRGB gamut investigation (flagged, not actioned)
nodes.rationale: 18.3% of 1825 pencils are sRGB-clipped (70.7% of those rescued under P3); several of the model's own anchors are themselves measurably chroma-clipped by the sRGB pipeline (e.g. the Lemon anchor loses ~13.7 points of true chroma via the sRGB round-trip) -- a legitimate future investigation, anchors remain locked on sRGB-derived hex throughout for now.

nodes.label: hexToLabD65()
nodes.rationale: Computes Lab always as D65 2° (Xn=0.95047 Yn=1.0 Zn=1.08883), not the master.json lab_d50_2 field directly, for consistency across the project.

nodes.label: mixTrueShare()/mixTrueEqual()
nodes.rationale: Solves for the mixing factors that give a TRUE concentration share, since spectral.js weights by factor^2 x tintingStrength^2 x luminance, not by the raw factor -- a naive equal-factor mix would not represent an equal pigment share.

nodes.label: spectral.js (Kubelka-Munk pigment mixing library, v3.0)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over RGB blending to mix as real pigments do (Kubelka-Munk), not flat colour averaging; v3.0 Color-class API used deliberately, not the old 2.0.2 flat-hex-string API.

nodes.label: Six canonical hue-role anchors (Warm Red, Warm Yellow, Cool Yellow, Cool Blue, Warm Blue, Cool Red)
nodes.norm_label: six canonical hue-role anchors (warm red, warm yellow, cool yellow, cool blue, warm blue, cool red)
nodes.rationale: RoY/YgB anchors use real measured pencils because they score better that way; BvR uses synthetic Munsell-derived anchors because BvR's coverage jumps substantially on synthetic anchors while RoY/YgB do best on real ones -- chosen per-arc by comparing all-real vs all-synthetic vs mixed against book-scope classification coverage.

nodes.label: Never-fit taxonomy (tint/tone/shade/neutral/etc.)
nodes.rationale: Classifies pencils that don't fit Level 1/2/3 by which Lab axis dominates the gap to the nearest model point (tint/shade/tone/neutral/high-neon/hue-gap), after first pulling out neutrals via Munsell chroma bands (not Lab chroma, which is unreliable both ways). Mirrors the book's own Ch5 tint/tone/shade structure deliberately.

nodes.label: Gamut-clipped anchor fix (2026-10-18)
nodes.rationale: Warm Yellow and Cool Blue were sRGB-gamut-clipped per master.json's own srgb_gamut_status field; spectral.Color(hex) re-estimates a reflectance curve from the already-clipped display hex, understating real pigment saturation in every downstream mix. Since Lab->XYZ->linear-RGB->gamma-encode is lossless reversible algebra with no inherent 0-255 bound, built new functions that construct the spectral.Color from the real measured Lab instead of the clipped hex, applied only to Level 1's first generation (where a raw anchor is mixed).

nodes.label: Shade-direction investigation (2026-10-17/18)
nodes.rationale: Shade (arc->black) rescues far worse than tint (arc->white) regardless of how many levels are added. A reverse-direction test (lighten the failing pencil's own colour toward white instead of darkening the arc) rescues 39/39, proving the hue/chroma identity is correct and only the construction DIRECTION is wrong. Root cause confirmed with real pigment Color Index data: high-tinting-strength pigments (PB15:3+PV23 etc.) get dark by stacking chroma, not by adding a neutral, and no substitute 'black' (pure #000000, realistic bone black #1C1814, or Holbein's near-true-neutral #262628) fixes it because different pencils are built from different dark pigments -- there's no single right answer to 'what black.' Conclusion: the arc->black construction itself needs rethinking, not which colour sits at its dark end.

nodes.label: BvR six-sector split (abandoned)
nodes.rationale: Splitting BvR into Blue-Violet + Violet-Red sub-arcs bridged by a shared midpoint looked better on a narrow pool-count metric (1796/1825 vs 1781/1825) but was visually wrong -- the new sub-arcs produced muddy, desaturated colour exactly at the seam, only visible in a rendered swatch, not caught by the metric. Abandoned in favour of a single synthetic BvR arc. Lesson: a fit-count metric can pass while the actual colour is wrong -- always confirm with a rendered swatch/diagram.

nodes.label: Cool Yellow anchor correction (2026-10-15)
nodes.rationale: Previous anchor #f6e83b read too warm/close to Warm Yellow by eye. A numbers-led first pass (4 candidates ranked by coverage cost) was rejected by Ray after testing real swatches against a live arc rendering -- 'none look right on the arc'. An eye-led second pass found Cadmium Yellow Lemon #e7ed46 (H=105.7°), confirmed by eye AND a genuine coverage gain (+11 book/+14 combined), unlike every earlier candidate which all cost coverage -- the only anchor change so far that didn't trade accuracy for appearance.

nodes.label: Warm Yellow anchor corrections (two rounds)
nodes.rationale: Started as Yellow Ochre (#f7c81e), chosen hue-precision-first; a systematic cross-brand gap (every pencil range missing a vivid 'Cadmium Yellow'-type pencil near the model's position) led to swapping to Lemon (#ffd200) 2026-10-04, then correcting a slipped hex to #ffd800 (Medium Cadmium Yellow Imit.) 2026-10-09, confirmed by Ray's own by-eye audit both times.

nodes.label: ADDED/DUPLICATE/CONFLICT dedup reporting
nodes.rationale: Identical hex is skipped safely (backfilling a missing URL); a same-identity-different-hex record is flagged as CONFLICT rather than silently overwritten, so a human checks which reading is correct. Idempotent across repeated/separate runs.
